extracted.intended_audience: experimental physiologists and chemists (Royal Society readers / researchers studying respiration and water analysis)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting, and reporting gas-exchange experiments on animals (here, pigeons) and chemical analyses of water, including apparatus description, measurements of gas volumes/composition, and interpretation of physiological and chemical changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe apparatus and reference prior descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The apparatus is engraved and described in the Phil. Trans. for 1809, page 429.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide diagrams/engravings and precise descriptions or citations of the apparatus used so others can reproduce the setup. Include capacities of vessels (intermediate glass vessel, gasometers), connecting tubes, and any quicksilver baths or stands used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report environmental conditions and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The barom. being 30.130, the therm. 54°, during 69 minutes ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record barometric pressure, temperature, and experiment duration; report times and temporal structure (intervals at which gases were supplied and samples taken).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify initial and final gas volumes and vessel capacities
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of the glass vessel was . 94 cubic inches. ... 587 cubic inches of air were supplied ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and report volumes/capacities of all vessels and the total volumes of gas present before and after the experiment. Include bulk/volume of the animal when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and report gas supply protocol (intervals and amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: At intervals of four or five minutes, 35 cubic inches at a time of common air were slowly passed through the vessel ... supplied every four minutes; during 22 minutes 75 cubic inches of oxygen gas were passed through ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how much gas was introduced at each interval, the timing between supplies, and any changes to that schedule during the run. This is necessary to link gas turnover to animal respiration and to compute rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and report appropriate chemical/gas analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The air respired was examined as usual, with lime water in the eudiometer with an elastic bottle, for carbonic acid, and with green sulphate of iron saturated with nitrous gas, for oxygen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify analytical reagents, instruments (eudiometer, Volta’s eudiometer), and procedures used to detect CO2, O2, H2, N2, etc. Report reagent conditions (e.g., saturated with nitrous gas) and any calibrations or validation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-check measurement consistency (register agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The registers of both gasometers agreed throughout to a very trifle, which confirmed our former observations ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple independent measures or registers and report their agreement to support measurement accuracy. Note any discrepancies and their magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and report animal behaviour and welfare indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: In about ten minutes the bird began to pant and became uneasy; the soft parts about his beak became of a bright red. ... on being released appeared very well, and did not seem at all injured by the experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record behavioral signs (panting, uneasiness, color changes, moisture on glass, use of beak/tongue, recovery on release) as indicators of distress or altered physiological state, and report whether the animal recovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report quantitative calculations and conversions explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Thus it appears that the bird produced about half a cubic inch of carbonic acid per minute; ... 100 cubic inches of carbonic acid contains 12.82 grains of carbon, the 35.80 cubic inches produced ... must contain 4.59 grains of carbon, or nearly at the rate of 96 grains in 24 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show arithmetic steps, constants used, per-minute and extrapolated per-24-hour rates, and conversions between gas volumes and mass (e.g., grains of carbon). This enables verification and comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare gas composition before and after and balance changes
rubrics_metrics.description: State of the air before the experiment: Atmospheric air 587 cubic inches, consisting of 123 oxygen, 464 azote. State after: 587 cubic inches, consisting of 35.80 carb. acid, 87.52 oxyg., 462.67 azote. ... when a larger proportion of oxygen ... is respired, a quantity of oxygen is absorbed by the blood, and an equal quantity of azote gas evolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full compositional breakdowns (O2, N2, CO2, H2) for the whole gas volume before and after. Compute increases/decreases and interpret physiological processes (oxygen absorption, nitrogen evolution, hydrogen loss).

rubrics_metrics.name: Run experiments across multiple gas compositions/conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: First experiment with atmospheric air. First experiment with oxygen gas. Second experiment with oxygen gas. Mixture of hydrogen and oxygen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the subject under different atmospheres (air, pure oxygen, oxygen/hydrogen mixtures) to isolate effects of gas composition on respiration and blood-gas exchange. Report each condition separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for and discuss measurement artifacts and uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: The difference is only 1.33, or little more than a cubic inch, which loss might have happened during the time the bird was uneasy; ... the volume of the gas was almost unaltered, but that there had been a great disturbance in the proportions of the azote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note possible sources of error (animal movement, condensation/moisture, timing of sampling), discuss their likely effects, and consider uncertainty when interpreting small differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe and describe physical/temporal phenomena (scum, sediment, bubbles) in water samples
rubrics_metrics.description: A quantity of black water subsided ... the sediment had risen to the surface, where it formed a pretty regular stratum ... to these, as well as to the scum itself, a number of minute air bubbles were attached ... after some time the masses again subsided, leaving the fluid almost totally free from any visible extraneous matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When studying spontaneous purification or other time-dependent processes, document visual changes (odour, colour, scum formation, bubbles), their timing, and any gas evolution associated with them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter and perform standard chemical analyses with quantitative reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When the process of depuration appeared to be complete, the water was filtered through paper, and ... 10,000 grains left by evaporation a saline crust ... By the appropriate tests, the water was found to contain lime, sulphuric acid, muriatic acid, and magnesia. There was a trace of alumine and an indication of potash; but no ammonia, sulphur, or iron could be detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter samples before chemical analysis; evaporate a known mass (e.g., 10,000 grains) to determine residue mass; apply appropriate qualitative tests for ions and acids; quantify salts (carbonate/sulphate/muriate etc.) and report amounts per standard mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present comparative tabulations and interpret compositional changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The respective quantities of these salts in 10,000 grains will be as follows: Carbonate of lime ... Sulphate of ditto ... Muriate of soda ... Muriate of magnesia ... The result of this analysis shows ... the quantity of saline matter is increased as much as four-fold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide before-and-after comparisons (tables or explicit lists) and interpret the significance (e.g., increase in salts, implications for suitability). Discuss which constituents increased or decreased and possible explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link experimental observations to physiological/chemical hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: These experiments ... prove that when atmospheric air alone is respired in a natural way, the proportion of azote is not altered, and that there is only a change of a certain portion of oxygen for an equal portion of carbonic acid gas; that when a larger proportion of oxygen ... is respired, a quantity of oxygen is absorbed by the blood, and an equal quantity of azote gas evolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured data to support or refute mechanistic hypotheses (e.g., blood absorbs oxygen and gives out nitrogen under oxygen-rich atmosphere). State clear conclusions tied to the quantitative results.
